intro: Google Docs runs in your browser, so on a Mac you open it in a browser such as Chrome and sign in. The ⌘ key replaces Ctrl for copy, paste and bold, and the citation tool sits under Tools > Citations. This guide covers the shortcuts, templates, citations and offline setup that matter for school work, plus where Lazur helps while you write.
tldr: Docs runs in a browser. Use Chrome or Edge if you want offline work on your Mac.
On Mac, ⌘ replaces Ctrl. Find and replace is ⌘⇧H, and word count is ⌘⇧C.
Templates sit in the Template Gallery, or under File > New > From a template.
Citations live under Tools > Citations, with MLA 8th, APA 7th and Chicago 17th author-date styles.
Lazur points, guides and explains while you work. It does not click buttons for you.

blocks.text: Google Docs on a Mac: what you need first
Google Docs runs in a browser, so there is nothing to install. Open Chrome or Edge, go to docs.google.com, and sign in with your Google account.
Choose Chrome or Edge if you plan to work offline. Google's offline help page names those two browsers. Safari is not on that list, so don't count on offline work there.
If you have more than one Google account, give each one its own browser profile. Offline access works for only one account per profile. The offline section below explains why.
If you come from Microsoft Word, expect some shortcuts to differ. Check Google's list before you assume a key works the same way.
Before a deadline, open the Tools menu and the Template Gallery once. If something is missing, your account type may be the reason. Ask your school IT team.
Google Docs keyboard shortcuts on Mac

Most Docs shortcuts match Windows, with one big change. Mac uses ⌘ (Command) where Windows uses Ctrl. Copy, paste and bold are the clearest examples. Learn ⌘C, ⌘V and ⌘B first, because you will press them in every paper.
Two shortcuts save more time than the rest for school work. Find and replace is ⌘⇧H, the same job as Ctrl+H on Windows. Word count is ⌘⇧C, which you need for any assignment with a length limit.

blocks.caption: Mac and Windows Docs shortcuts, from Google's keyboard shortcut help page.

blocks.text: Press ⌘/ to open the full shortcut list. Search it for the action you need, instead of memorizing everything at once.
A common mistake is pressing Ctrl out of habit. On a Mac, make ⌘ your default for the basic keys first. Add the rest as you need them.
Three shortcuts to practice this week

items: ⌘C, ⌘V and ⌘B: copy, paste and bold, the basics in every paper.
⌘⇧H: find and replace, useful when a term changes across a long essay.
⌘⇧C: word count, your last check before you submit.
⌘/: the full list, when you forget a shortcut.

blocks.text: Templates for class notes, to-do lists and reading lists
Start in the Template Gallery. On the Docs home screen, it sits at the top right. Inside a document, go to File > New > From a template to open the same gallery.

Google's help page says some template features are only available for work or school accounts. A personal Gmail account may show fewer options. Check what your account shows before you build a study plan around one template.

Three templates suit student work. Class Notes gives you tabbed sections for takeaways and homework. To-Do List and Reading List cover deadlines and the books you need to finish. A TCEA post dated February 27, 2025 describes these as pageless templates. TCEA is a third-party education blog, not Google.

Google's help page does not describe student-specific templates. It lists reading list and class notes options for education users, and that is as specific as it gets. Read the TCEA post for the layout, then check the gallery on your own account.
Setting up Class Notes for one lecture

items: Open File > New > From a template and pick Class Notes.
Rename the doc with the course code and the lecture date, so you can find it later.
Use the tabbed sections. Put key ideas in one tab and homework in another.
If typing falls behind, hold fn and dictate. Then read the text back and fix the punctuation.

blocks.text: Keep one class notes doc per course. A single long file for every subject becomes hard to search by midterm week.
Citations in Google Docs: MLA, APA and Chicago on Mac

The citation tool lives under Tools > Citations. It supports three styles: MLA (8th ed.), APA (7th ed.) and Chicago Author-Date (17th ed.). Pick the style your instructor names, not the one you like best.
Add each source through the citation panel. When your references are done, place the cursor where the list belongs. Then press the Insert bibliography button in the sidebar.
Check the edition before you cite. The tool lists MLA 8th edition, not 9th. If your class follows the 9th edition, check each entry by hand against your style guide.

blocks.title: English only
blocks.text: Google's help page says the elements the tool generates only appear in English at this time. If your paper or your sources are in another language, check every generated entry by hand.

The help page also does not list the source types the tool supports. Test one book entry and one website entry before you add a full reference list. A short test takes little time. A wrong format can cost you points.
Citation mistakes that cost points

items: Choosing a style from memory. Check the assignment sheet, since MLA, APA and Chicago differ in format and edition.
Assuming the tool covers the newest edition. The help page lists MLA 8th edition, not 9th.
Waiting until the last night to build the bibliography. Generated entries still need a read.
Skipping the English-only limit when a paper is written in another language.

blocks.text: Offline Google Docs on Mac: setup and limits
Offline Docs needs an internet connection to set up. After that, you can keep working when the connection drops. That helps on a train or in a building with weak Wi-Fi.
Turn it on in Chrome or Edge, in a normal window. Google's help page says you can set it up in Drive Settings under Offline, or from the document status icon.

items: Open Chrome or Edge in a regular window and sign in to the right account.
Open Drive settings and turn on Offline, or use the document status icon in Docs.
Open a doc, turn Wi-Fi off, and check that it opens and accepts typing.
Repeat the Wi-Fi check before a trip, a commute or a library day with bad signal.

blocks.text: Two limits catch students. First, only one account per browser profile can have offline enabled. Create a second Chrome or Edge profile for each extra account.

Second, a school can block offline access. Administrators can turn it off, and the error reads Offline sync is disabled by your administrator. You cannot fix that setting yourself, so ask your IT help desk.

blocks.title: Test on a quiet day
blocks.text: Run the Wi-Fi off check on a day with no deadline. If the setting is blocked, you still have time to ask IT or pick another plan.
Gemini in Google Docs: where it lives and what to check
On April 22, 2026, Google added a bottom bar and a side panel as the main Gemini entry points in Docs. Google's update says you can prompt Gemini from either one.
On February 12, 2026, Google added Listen to document summary to the Tools menu. Use Tools > Listen to document summary when you want the document read back to you.
On May 4, 2026, Google added custom instructions for Gemini in Docs. You set them in the side panel, and you can keep up to 1,000 active instructions.
Gemini output is a draft, not a source. Check each claim against the reading, and cite the original author. Never cite the chatbot as your source.
Your school may control which Gemini features are on. Ask your instructor or IT team before you rely on one for graded work.
Group projects in one shared doc
Decide who owns each section before anyone types. Shared docs go faster when each person knows which part is theirs.
Put the citation list in one place. If two people add references with different tools or styles, the bibliography will mix formats. Agree on one style at the first meeting.
Keep one final copy that nobody else edits. That copy is the version you submit, so you can point to it if someone changes text at the last minute.
What the research says about students and Google Docs

A 2026 study of 41 university students found a positive view of Google Docs. It used purposive sampling, which means the researchers picked students on purpose rather than at random. The mean score was 3.217, and the scale is not stated, so read it as a direction, not a grade.
No verified survey measures how many students struggle with Docs on a Mac. Slowness reports appear in forum posts. This guide does not count them as facts, so test the doc on your own machine.

Google's 2025 year in review says Gemini for Education reached more than 10 million students across more than 1,000 US higher education institutions. That figure covers Gemini, not Docs, so do not read it as Docs usage.
Ask Lazur while you write in Google Docs on Mac
Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch on your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘, which means Option and Command together, to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud.
Lazur sees your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Three uses fit Docs well. Ask where the Tools menu is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to start a bibliography, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor.
Lazur does not click buttons or edit your file for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Google Docs. It works in any app on your Mac, and you stay in control of every click and every word.
For the Docs side of this, see [Google Docs help with Lazur](/apps/google-docs). For the wider study setup, see [Lazur for students](/for/students).
Common mistakes students make in Google Docs on Mac

items: Pressing Ctrl out of habit. Switch to ⌘ for the basic keys and keep the shortcut table nearby.
Trying to set up offline access in a private or incognito window. Offline setup does not work there.
Signing in to two accounts in one browser profile. Offline access works for only one of them.
Trusting a Gemini summary without reading the original text.
Formatting references by hand when Tools > Citations already offers your style.
Testing offline access for the first time on the day of a deadline.

blocks.text: A worked example: finishing a cited paper on Mac

items: Write the body of the paper first. Keep a short list of sources at the bottom as you read.
Add each source through Tools > Citations, choosing the style your instructor named.
Put your cursor where the references go, then press Insert bibliography in the sidebar.
Press ⌘⇧C for word count, and check it against the limit on the assignment sheet.
Read the bibliography from top to bottom. Fix any entry that looks wrong before you submit.

blocks.text: Work through the list in order, and stop after each step to check it. A quick read at the end catches the errors the tool cannot know about, such as a wrong title or a missing page range.
Next steps before your next deadline

items: Practice ⌘C, ⌘V, ⌘B and ⌘⇧H on one page this week.
Save the Class Notes template for each course.
Turn on offline access in Chrome or Edge, then run the Wi-Fi off test.
Check the citation style on your assignment sheet before you open Tools > Citations.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur out loud where the word count is.

blocks.text: If focus is the real problem, read [losing focus while studying on a laptop](/for/students/problems/losing-focus-while-studying-on-a-laptop). For a study routine around your writing, see the [AI study buddy for students](/blog/ai-study-buddy-for-students) post.

faq.question: Does Google Docs work on a Mac in any browser?
faq.answer: Google Docs runs in a browser, so you use it on a Mac without installing an app. Offline work is different. It requires Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, and it does not work in private or incognito windows.

faq.question: What is the Mac shortcut for find and replace in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Press ⌘⇧H. On Windows the same job uses Ctrl+H. Press ⌘/ to see the full list of shortcuts and search it for anything else you need.

faq.question: How do I add MLA citations in Google Docs on a Mac?
faq.answer: Open Tools > Citations, choose MLA (8th ed.), and add each source. Then place your cursor where the list belongs and use the Insert bibliography button in the sidebar. The tool lists the 8th edition, so check whether your class wants 9th.

faq.question: Can I use offline Google Docs with a school account and a personal account?
faq.answer: Yes, but in separate browser profiles. Only one account per browser profile can have offline enabled. Create a second Chrome or Edge profile for the other account and set up offline there.

faq.question: Why can't I turn on offline Docs?
faq.answer: Your school administrator may block offline access. The error reads Offline sync is disabled by your administrator. You cannot change that setting yourself, so ask your IT help desk.

faq.question: Are the Google Docs templates the same for every account?
faq.answer: Not always. Google's help page says some template features are only for work or school accounts. Open File > New > From a template to see what your own account shows.

faq.question: Does Lazur write my paper in Google Docs?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text when you ask, and it points, guides and explains. It does not click buttons or edit files for you, so you still decide what goes in the paper.

faq.question: Is my screen recorded when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
